content: The wound is the place where the light enters you.
author: Rumi
story: In 1244, Rumi was an esteemed Islamic theologian and orthodox jurist in Konya until he met Shams-i-Tabrizi, an enigmatic wandering dervish. When Shams mysteriously vanished—likely murdered by envious disciples—Rumi was cast into an inconsolable abyss of bereavement. Rather than collapsing under grief, Rumi channeled this shattering agony into ecstatic poetry and devotional dance, discovering that sorrow fractures the rigid shell of the ego so divine illumination can flood inside. The wound was not his ruin; it was the sacred doorway to his awakening.
reflectionPrompt: What painful fracture or disappointment from your past eventually carved out the capacity for your deepest wisdom and compassion today?
